payload.blocks: Phases 2 and 3, and through them phases 4, 6, 8, 9 and 10 (acceptance criterion 4, every door debt gone). Phases 1, 5 and 7 continue.
payload.headline: Component-authority-doors phases 2-3 need callers outside the plan footprint: re-cut per row, widen, or cut scope?

parts.cause: Unit reports in plans/261121-2110-component-authority-doors/reports/unit-261123-0819-p02-result.md and -p03-result.md, spot-checked with rg at 94db955. Phase 3: 9 source files (bin/fgos.mjs, src/session-host/head-start.mjs, src/workflow/propose.mjs and others) and about 110 test files import the twins. Phase 2: scripts/fgos-session-start-hook.mjs, src/verbs/merge/iron-law-level.mjs, the frozen mailbox v7e/v7h/v7i hashes, and a crate edge in packages/herdr-fgos-common/rust/Cargo.toml.

options.cost: About one planner wake (plan files only). No code changes until the new phases run.
options.does: The planner splits phases 2-4 (and re-checks 6, 8, 9) into one phase per door row, each with its callers in the footprint. The frozen mailbox rows and the herdr crate edge become their own backlog items or wait on their owning lane.
options.gain: Each retirement lands as one small commit with all of its callers moved, so CA-D2 holds. Small footprints collide less with other plans at admission.
options.harm: The plan goes back to planning for those phases, and there are more phases to run.
options.label: A. Planner re-cuts the retirement phases per row

options.cost: A footprint edit by the planner or supervisor. The two phases are probably several thousand lines of diff.
options.does: Adds the roughly 25 source and 110 test files listed in the reports to the footprint, and reruns phases 2 and 3 as two large phases.
options.gain: No re-planning, and the fastest path to running again.
options.harm: Two very large commits. The footprint overlaps most running and ready plans, so admission will hold them, and the frozen mailbox hashes still need their lane's re-measurement.
options.label: B. Widen the footprint as is and rerun 2 and 3

options.cost: About 2 small units, plus a scope change to the plan.
options.does: Delivers the rows that need no outside caller (execution-doctor-judgments, person-agent-config-writes and maybe decide-a-dispatch). The other rows stay as debt in new backlog items.
options.harm: Breaks the plan outcome and acceptance criterion 4 (every debt gone, schema without debt), so phase 10 cannot finish as written.
options.label: C. Retire only in-footprint rows, defer the rest

parts.recommendation: A: per-row phases keep the no-twin rule (CA-D2) and the commits small, and they do not freeze other plans out at admission. Until you answer, the lead runs phases 1, 5 and 7, which do not depend on 2 or 3.

scope.allows: A planner to re-cut phases 2-4, 6, 8 and 9 of this plan and to widen the footprint by exactly the callers of each row it plans; new backlog rows for the frozen mailbox rows and the herdr crate edge.
scope.forbids: Changing the plan outcome or acceptance criteria, dropping any door row, or the lead editing the footprint itself.

parts.what: Phase 2 (setup/CLI twins) and phase 3 (dispatch twins) both stopped without changing anything. Retiring a twin means moving all of its callers, and most callers sit outside the plan footprint. The lead may not widen the footprint.
